Azeroth is home to a wide variety of beasts. From the new world of
Lordaeron to the old world of Kalimdor, all manner of creatures can be found.
Some are friendly, some are ferocious and aggressive - yet they all have one thing
in common. Each creature shares a special connection with Hunters. Hunters track,
tame and slay all manner of animals and beasts found in the wilds. Whether they
rely on bows or firearms, Hunters consider their weapons and pets to be their
only true friends.
1.
Comprehensive Guide to Hunter in World of Warcraft: Forever
Hunter is the lone survivalist, using animal companions, traps, and mastery with a ranged
weapon to deal with anything that comes your way. The core fantasy of a Hunter lies in its role
as a ranger, combined with access to a wide array of utility such as tracking, traps, animal handling,
misdirection, and numerous crowd control options to always stay in control of a fight. Hunters
thrive in a solo fight and are widely considered one of the best solo classes in the game, especially
when it comes to leveling. Tame a companion, take aim as a master marksman, and lie in wait
to deliver the first blow before anyone knows what hit them.
If you are planning to play Hunter, make sure to check back often as Blizzard
continues tuning the class.

Hunter Guides
Forge a bond with a loyal beast and fight as one, overwhelming your enemies with the strength of your companion.

Hunter in World of Warcraft: Forever
Beast Mastery Hunter
Marksmanship Hunter
Survival Hunter
Beast Mastery functions mostly the same, heavily relying on your pet to become the main source
of your damage while also tanking enemies out in the world. The main new addition is the talent
Summon Hawk
. Summon Hawk shares a cooldown with
Arcane Shot
and will summon a hawk that attacks your enemy for up to 18 seconds. You can only have two hawks active
at any time in addition to your pet. The Beast Mastery rotation will focus on always keeping
two hawks active while weaving shots in-between uses.
Leveling Information
Beast Mastery Hunter Guides

Go to Guide
Marksmanship is relatively unchanged from the traditional Classic Hunter apart from the
quality of life additions mentioned above. The primary new ability for Marksmanship is their
capstone talent
Sniper Shot
, which is a massive shot with a 4-second cast time.
Because of its excessive cast time, it's possible this ability will actually be a damage loss in PvE,
but it will be an extremely strong ability for any time you need burst damage.
Marksmanship also has the
Lone Wolf
talent early in its tree. This gives
you a 20% damage boost if you do not have an active pet. This is both a large damage buff
and can give players an option for if you do not want to worry about micromanaging your
pet in dungeons and raids.

be a primarily melee based spec, with talents like
Savage Strikes
and
Predator's Edge
massively boosting your melee damage, specifically while dual-wielding. They also get access to the new
ability
Strider Kick
as another rotational melee ability, along with
Expose Prey
and
Lacerating Strikes
which make
Mongoose Bite

stronger ability that you can actually use more frequently. Overall Survival looks extremely promising,
especially with talents like

Welcome to our Beast Mastery Hunter Ranged DPS guide
    for WoW Forever, tailored for PvE content. Here, you will learn how all you
    need to know to play the
    Hunter class as Beast Mastery Ranged DPS. Click the links
    #below to navigate the guide
    or read this page for a short introduction.
Table of Contents
1. Compendium of Beast Mastery Hunter Information for the World of Warcraft: Forever Beta
2. Level 30 Talent Build
3. Beast Mastery Hunter Spells and Rotation
4. Level 30 Gear, Stat Priority, and Consumables
1.
Compendium of Beast Mastery Hunter Information for the World of Warcraft: Forever Beta
Hunter is your classic ranger archetype, setting traps and dealing damage
from afar while relying on your powerful animal companion to deal unrelenting damage and
keep your enemy's focus. Beast Mastery is the specialization that heavily invests into your pet;
your pet becomes not only your primary source of damage but also acts as your tank out in
the world, making it one of the best solo and leveling specializations in the game. Hunters
have an iconic, versatile toolkit that enables them to trap, control, and attack enemies on
their own schedule while your pet stays up close and personal to deal devastating damage.
Beast Mastery Hunters are entering World of Warcraft Forever with a familiar package to
what Hunters had in Classic, but with some powerful new upgrades and a couple of new tools
that double down on your pet-based identity. The big addition which you get access to at level
25 is
Summon Hawk
which will be one of your new core rotational abilities.
This allows you to summon a hawk to attack your target, with a maximum of two hawks active
at any time. The other major change is that your pet now has scaling with your stats like in later
version of World of Warcraft, which means Beast Mastery will continue to grow in power
even deep into raids at max level.
Overall Performance
Leveling
Dungeon
Utility
Mobility
Easy to Learn, Hard to Master
Hunters have one of the strongest skill floors in the game, and Beast Mastery perfectly plays
to that strength by placing more power into your pet. It enables any player to blaze through the
leveling process with far more power than other classes offer early on. However, Hunters
still have an exceptional amount of depth and optimization for the best players to really showcase
their skill. Hunters overall lack some of the AoE and cleave damage options that separates out
the true DPS powerhouses like Warriors, but still offer exceptional damage and a versatile utility
package that makes them an excellent all-rounder even into the end-game.
Top-tier leveling
Beast Mastery Hunters simply offers the complete package for leveling. By investing into the
strength of your pet, you have your own personal relentless tank capable of not only holding
threat, but dealing immense damage. You can always heal it yourself, re-summon as needed,
and support it from afar with your own exceptional damage. Even with no mana, you still deal
extremely competitive damage with just a basic
Auto Shot
and a pet. Finally,
Hunters have one of the best tools in the game for leveling with
Feign Death
,
giving you an option to reset and escape combat if you ever end up in a bad situation. Hunters
overall are the strongest leveling class in World of Warcraft, and Beast Mastery is the specialization
that doubles down on that strength for leveling.
Strong, Persistent Damage
While Hunters posses the complete package for solo game play, that strength is far less important
in a dungeon where you have allies to cover other roles. Beast Mastery Hunters are still a strong
choice with the combination of excellent single target damage and on-demand AOE with
Explosive Trap
and
Multi-Shot
. Hunters additionally have
extremely useful crowd control with
Freezing Trap
and
Frost Trap
.
As a final note, you always need to take extra care with pet control in dungeons to ensure you
are not accidentally pulling additional targets; an irresponsible Hunter quickly becomes a liability in some dungeons.
A Versatile Utility Package
While Hunters do not have the strongest crowd control spells possible, they have solid options
available that make up a versatile package.
Freezing Trap
and
Frost Trap
in particular are extremely useful in dungeons for targeted and AoE control. Beast Mastery Hunters
also gain
Intimidation
as an on-use stun that is extremely strong for interrupting
enemies and locking them down.
Finally,
Feign Death
is one of the best possible panic buttons for any sort of
dangerous content.
Fast, but Delicate
Hunters have their iconic aspects, including
Aspect of the Cheetah
which
is their primary mobility spell. They can move 30% faster, increasing even further with talents.
This can be toggled on at any time, even in combat, which makes it extremely valuable and allows
Hunters to kite effectively. However, the major downside here is that while Cheetah is active,
taking any damage dazes you and removes the aspect. Hunters have exceptional kiting potential,
but it's a dual-edge sword with a large downside that has to be used carefully.
Starter Information
Beginner Guides
New to the game? Get started with our Leveling guide!
Leveling
2.
Level 30 Talent Build
Hunter has a couple of very strong early talents, 
but Beast Mastery unlocks its most valuable talents
from levels 20 to 30. To start, you should absolutely 
take
Deadly Aspects
in the Beast
Mastery tree. This is one of the best 5 point talents 
you can take, especially early on, since it allows
you to proc a 30% haste buff for 12 seconds.
Once you put 5 points into Deadly Aspects, you absolutely should put two points into
Pathfinding
. While this is not a DPS talent, the extra 6% movement speed
is going to be so much more noticeable than anything else while you run around the world
without a mount.
The remaining 4 points at Level 20 are far more subjective.
Improved Revive Pet
is a great general option early on since it makes
Revive Pet
both far stronger
and more reliable to use even in a combat situation, allowing you to reliably bring your pet back
if it ever dies.
Focused Fire
is the strongest DPS talent available at this point,
with
Lethal Attacks
as a close second.
Hawk Eye
is another
solid option just to give you extra range for kiting, especially if PvP is your goal. Finally, if you put
all 10 points into Beast Mastery,
Bestial Swiftness
is a really strong quality of
life talent point both for leveling and for PvP since your pet will be able to move far quicker between
targets.
Finally, from 20 to 30 you should max out
Unleashed Fury
for the additional
damage before taking
Summon Hawk
as soon as it is available. This will be
your most important unlock and is a new core rotational ability, effectively giving you two more
pets to keep active. With the remaining points up to Level 30, you can take 3 points in
Ferocity
before taking
Intimidation
. You can also choose to not take either middle
talent, choosing instead to go for the full 5 points in Ferocity. This is a higher DPS option, but spending
2 points for the on-use stun and extra pet movement speed is absolutely worth it for general
quality of life.
2.1.
Legacy Points
At this point, you also could potentially have up to 5 extra talent points if you unlocked
every Legacy Point bonus available. The best option here would be to finish out the full 5 points
in
Ferocity
, followed by 2 points in
Bestial Discipline
and 1 point in
Frenzy
. These are all highly impactful points and absolutely
worth picking up as soon as possible. You could choose to put them elsewhere, but you will want
to respec later on anyways to grab
Bestial Wrath
once you have 31 points available,
so it is better to just stay fully in Beast Mastery.
2.2.
Best Races For Beast Mastery Hunter
Horde
: Tauren –
the single strongest
choice out of any race across both factions for Hunter, entirely due to
Plainsrunning
.
As a Hunter, you can run continuously to build up 30% movement speed while even at Level 1,
then stutter step while attacking from range to use
Auto Shot
. This enables you
to kill any target from range while leveling without ever taking melee hits, even at Level 1. While
this buff does not stack with
Aspect of the Cheetah
later, it still allows you to keep
30% movement speed if managed well while keeping
Aspect of the Hawk
up,
which is a major DPS boost. Beyond that, Taurens still get an additional 5% max health and 1%
hit chance with
Endurance
and an on-use AoE stun with
War Stomp
.
Alliance
: Human –
for the Alliance,
the choice of racials is far closer so you should feel free to pick whichever one fits your personal
preference. However, Humans will offer a slight edge in both PvP and PvE.
Will to Survive
is an invaluable panic button to break stuns, which in PvP is when you are in the most danger against
melee that connect with you.
Perception
also provides another tool to look
for stealthed targets. Finally, the major DPS increase comes from
Sword Specialization
,
which causes you to gain 2% crit chance as long as your melee weapons include at least 1 sword. It is
important to note that this generally increases your crit chance, so it will also apply the bonus to your
ranged attacks.
3.
Beast Mastery Hunter Spells and Rotation
The Hunter rotation is incredibly simple early on, almost entirely relying on the strength of
Auto Shot
to kill enemies. First and foremost, always have
Aspect of the Hawk
active before engaging with something unless you are actively kiting it away and need the speed bonus
of
Aspect of the Cheetah
. Before Level 10, you should also focus on moving backwards
between Auto Shots since you want to maximize the number of times you attack a target from range
before it reaches your dead-zone and gets into melee.
Put
Hunter's Mark
up on your target before combat.
Command your pet to attack your target first, with its abilities on auto-cast.
Once your pet damages and attacks your target, start with
Serpent Sting
.
Summon Hawk
on cooldown, always keeping 2 hawks active.
Aimed Shot
on cooldown.
Continue to
Auto Shot
your target.
If you ever pull aggro away from your pet, use
Disengage
.
If you find yourself capped on mana and will have 2 hawks active for more than 6 seconds, use
Arcane Shot
.
Auto Shot
the enemy until it dies.
Against multiple enemies, use
Multi-Shot
instead of
Aimed Shot
.
As a final reminder, the majority of a Hunter's power comes from both you and your pet's basic attacks.
Even if you are out of mana, it will always be more efficient to just attack the next target and
regenerate your mana slowly while using basic attacks. Prioritize using
Mend Pet
to heal your pet along with
Serpent Sting
to efficiently utilize your mana.
3.1.
Pets
At Level 10, you will have the ability to tame a pet. This is the single greatest leveling tool
that any class gets without exception. Hunters have always had the ability to tame a pet, but there
are a couple of important distinctions from Classic that are worth noting.
Pets have one of three classifications: Ferocity, Cunning, or Tenacity.
Pets do not have an inherent damage buff or reduction based on type.
Pet happiness and loyalty still exists; remember to feed your pet!
Pets inherit some of your stats, which means they gain power along with you.
Every pet family, such as cats or turtles, has its own unique ability.
To level up pet abilities, you still need to go out and tame a higher level pet that already
    knows the skill you are looking for. Your pet will not naturally learn higher level abilities on
    its own.
Once you do train higher level pet abilities, you can then teach it to any other pet in the future
	that is capable of learning that ability.
For leveling, Bears are a generally strong choice. They are a defensive pet capable of tanking
well, but most importantly have access to a unique Swipe ability. A Bear's Swipe has a 5-second
cooldown and deals cleave damage in front of them, which makes it one of the rare pet abilities
capable of dealing consistent AoE damage to hold aggro on multiple targets.
3.2.
Utility and Unique Tools
Hunters are known for a variety of unique utility tools that are both incredibly useful
and flavorful for the class.
Hunters can track different types of enemies on the mini-map through various tracking skills.
Hunters can always keep an aspect buff up, which notably includes
Aspect of the Cheetah
.
  This is one of the rare movement speed buffs available before you get a mount.
Feign Death
will cause you to play dead, causing any nearby enemies
  to drop threat on you and reset. However, they will still attack your pet if it is alive and nearby.
  This is one of the most valuable leveling spells for resetting and leaving combat if things get too dangerous.
Freezing Trap
will freeze an enemy in a block of ice when triggered, providing
  a reliable way to keep one target locked down.
Frost Trap
leaves a patch of frost on an area, massively slowing down
  targets inside.
Concussive Shot
is an instant-cast, single-target slow. This is one of the
  strongest tools a Hunter has in PvP, especially against melee.
Disengage
can be used to lower your threat on a target.
4.
Level 30 Gear, Stat Priority, and Consumables
While leveling up to 30, generally you should go for the highest level items that follow the stat
priority listed below. Look out for pieces with high amounts of Agility specifically, high level weapons,
and rare quality gear wherever you can. The best items available will come from a combination
of dungeon quests, dungeon boss drops, crafted pieces, and other quest chain rewards.
At Level 20, some of the best gear comes from the Wailing Caverns dungeon. This includes
the
Venomstrike
bow along with the full Fang set, with pieces such as
Leggings of the Fang
.
At level 30, the difference in most slots is relatively minor as well.  However, there are a few
notable outliers for what is available.
Truthseeker's Bow
is an incredible
low level bow that you can pick up as a quest reward.
Leatherworking
has some strong pieces available from crafting, including the chest
Dusky Leather Armor
.
Triprunner Dungarees
are a quest reward from one of the Gnomeregan
dungeon quests. Finally,
Armor Piercer
gives more Agility than any other weapon
combination and is a common boss drop from Razorfen Kraul.
4.1.
Stat Priority
The stat priority boils down to two things: get the highest damage weapons possible and
get as much Agility as possible. Beyond that, you generally will just want the highest level
gear possible while leveling. Below is a more detailed explanation of the various stats
for Beast Mastery Hunter and the benefits they provide.
Weapon Damage
Far and away your most important stat. Keep in mind, weapons have both a DPS value
	and a damage value; slower weapons will hit harder, but less often. While you usually will just
	prefer the higher level weapon, slower weapons are better overall since you want a weapon
	that deals more damage per individual hit. This is because your abilities such as
Aimed Shot
calculate their base damage from your weapon's damage, meaning your abilities do more
	damage with a higher damage weapon.
Hit
You have a baseline chance to miss attacks, which increases as you face higher level enemies.
	Getting hit chance makes you less likely to miss. This stat is strong, but is also generally not
	ever found on low level gear.
Agility
Increases both your attack power and crit chance per point. In general, Hunters gain the
	majority of their scaling from Agility, which makes this your most important primary stat. You
	should be looking to have this on every piece of gear.
Critical Strike
Critical strikes deal bonus damage and provide bonus effects through certain talents, such
	as your
Frenzy
talent, which causes your pets to gain attack speed when they deal critical strikes.
	More importantly, pets also inherit your critical strike chance, meaning crit is a direct damage
	buff to both you and your pet.
Intellect
Each point provides one Attack Power through
Careful Aim
, while
	also increasing your maximum mana. With Careful Aim talented this is your next most important
	stat after Agility. Having a higher mana pool is also incredibly important generally just
	to ensure you can cast more spells without stopping in a single fight.
Spirit
Increases your base mana regeneration and your out of combat health regeneration rates.
	This is a valuable leveling stat since it will cause you to recover more
	mana faster. However, this is only for leveling; Stamina and Intellect are far more valuable
	for both survivability and actual combat capacity.
Stamina
Each point increases your maximum health. Having a large health pool is important
	for just being more durable, but as a Hunter you generally should not be tanking or taking
	damage. This is your least important stat while leveling, but pets also gain more max health
	per point of stamina you have as well.
4.2.
Consumables
While leveling, the most important consumables are going to be the highest level food you
can eat for health regeneration, water for mana regeneration, and health potions as an emergency
defensive button. While you can look into elixirs and other buff foods, you do not need to focus
on them too much while leveling unless you are trying to optimize significantly.
That being said, there are some easy elixirs you can get to help with your base power while
leveling.
Elixir of Agility
along with other variations of the straight Agility
elixirs are going to be the most noticeable damage increase, and quite cost efficient while leveling
once you have some gold to spare. Since you are leveling with a pet, you do not need to worry
too much about survivability; any buffs should primarily focus on damage.
Another important consumable will be bandages from
First Aid
. First
Aid gives you something to use your cloth on while leveling, and provides an incredibly strong
way of healing yourself both in and out of combat. It is highly recommended to keep your First
Aid skill current while leveling.
4.3.
Campfire Buffs
One of the incredible new additions in World of Wacraft Forever is campsites. You can
set up Campsites yourself, or look for them out in the world to sit by a campfire for the campfire
buffs. Different professions can offer buffs, all of which generally correspond to the possible
class buffs. These are incredibly strong while leveling, so if you ever seen players sitting around
a campfire out in the world, make sure to stop by to sit and get some buffs.

Hunter is your classic ranger archetype, setting traps and dealing damage
from afar while relying on your powerful animal companion to deal unrelenting damage and
keep your enemy's focus. Marksmanship is the specialization that heavily invests into your own
ranged damage, enabling you to deal devastating hits from further away than anyone else. While
you still have a pet, traps, and other tools to rely on, ultimately your strongest asset is going
to be the massive hits that bombard your enemies.
Marksmanship Hunters have a very similar play style in World of Warcraft Forever compared
to what Hunters had in Classic, but with some exciting new upgrades that double down on your
identity as a marksman. Marksmanship has a new pinnacle talent,
Sniper Shot
,
which is an extremely powerful shot on a 4-second cooldown that will enable you to deal
more burst damage than ever before, but only when you have the time and space to see it through.
Overall Performance
Leveling
Dungeon
Utility
Mobility
Easy to Learn, Hard to Master
Hunters have one of the strongest skill floors in the game, but Marksmanship also has one of
the highest skill ceilings. Hunters have the combination of melee and ranged attacks in their
arsenal, then the addition of extremely powerful attacks like
Sniper Shot
which deal devastating damage, but requires you to have perfect setup in a fight to get the
most use out of it. Hunters lack some of the AoE and cleave damage options that separates out
the true DPS powerhouses like Warriors, but still offer exceptional damage and a versatile utility
package that makes them an excellent all-rounder even into the end-game.
Top-tier leveling
Hunters in general offer the strongest setup for leveling thanks to the combination of your pet
and extremely efficient ranged attacks. Marksmanship invests more into your own strength,
beefing up your ranged damage and ensuring that you kill enemies faster. Hunters are still exceptional,
top-tier levelers so this setup will work out just fine, but this is overall slightly worse than investing
more into your pet. Your pet is still going to be your most important asset while leveling, which
makes Beast Mastery slightly better. Regardless, the combination alone of just
Auto Shot
and a pet is better than what most other classes can provide while leveling.
Strong, Persistent Damage
While Hunters posses the complete package for solo game play, that strength is far less important
in a dungeon where you have allies to cover other roles. Marksmanship Hunters are still a strong
choice with the combination of excellent single target damage and on-demand AOE with
Explosive Trap
and
Multi-Shot
. Marksmanship also invests
further into this strength, especially with talents that boost the damage benefit given to your own
attacks and Multi-Shot specifically. You still have the standard Hunter utility kit with abilities such
as
Frost Trap
, but your AoE damage especially is the highest of any Hunter
specialization.
A Versatile Utility Package
While Hunters do not have the strongest crowd control spells possible, they have solid options
available that make up a versatile package.
Freezing Trap
and
Frost Trap
in particular are extremely useful in dungeons for targeted and AoE control.
Finally,
Feign Death
is one of the best possible panic buttons for any sort of
dangerous content. Marksmanship Hunters also have the added option to take
Scatter Shot
as a late talent, but this is only ever going to be useful in PvP.
Fast, but Delicate
Hunters have their iconic aspects, including
Aspect of the Cheetah
which
is their primary mobility spell. They can move 30% faster, increasing even further with talents.
This can be toggled on at any time, even in combat, which makes it extremely valuable and allows
Hunters to kite effectively. However, the major downside here is that while Cheetah is active,
taking any damage dazes you and removes the aspect. Hunters have exceptional kiting potential,
but it's a dual-edge sword with a large downside that has to be used carefully. This is even
more important for Marksmanship Hunters, since a far larger portion of your damage potential
is gutted if you are forced into melee range.
Starter Information
Beginner Guides
New to the game? Get started with our Leveling guide!
Leveling
2.
Level 30 Talent Build
At Level 30 you only get 21 talent points 
total, which limits your options for going deep into
any one tree. This also means that you have more 
freedom with taking points in any specialization.
For Hunters, the single best starting talent is
Deadly Aspects
. However, this build
above instead focuses in on going 21 points deep 
into Marksmanship to get
Lone Wolf
and
Trueshot Aura
.
This build is not a good general play build. If you 
want a far better general build for just existing
in the world, you should use the Beast Mastery 
build at this level instead to take Deadly
Aspects and
Pathfinding
. If you 
want to go deep into Marksmanship,
the best use-case for it is for Dungeons, 
specifically to maximize your AoE damage and benefit to a party with Trueshot Aura.
At low level, you should never take
Lone Wolf
unless your goal is
to maximize your cleave and AoE damage in dungeons. If all you care about is dungeon performance,
then an extra 20% damage is excellent to buff your
Multi-Shot
. Finally,
Mortal Shots
is also a fantastic damage increase, making your critical hits
more deadly.
2.1.
Legacy Points
At this point, you also could potentially have up to 5 extra talent points if you unlocked
every Legacy Point bonus available. At this point at level 30, there are two options for where
these additional points could go for Marksmanship. First, you could just choose to put all 5 points
into
Deadly Aspects
. This is a high DPS option and is probably the best choice
knowing that your beta characters will never level past 30. Long-term,
Rapid Recuperation
is going to be a far better option for solving mana issues, and lets you go deeper into the Marksmanship
tree to eventually take
Sniper Shot
if you were planning a full leveling route.
2.2.
Best Races For Marksmanship Hunter
Horde
: Tauren –
the single strongest
choice out of any race across both factions for Hunter, entirely due to
Plainsrunning
.
As a Hunter, you can run continuously to build up 30% movement speed while even at Level 1,
then stutter step while attacking from range to use
Auto Shot
. This enables you
to kill any target from range while leveling without ever taking melee hits, even at Level 1. While
this buff does not stack with
Aspect of the Cheetah
later, it still allows you to keep
30% movement speed if managed well while keeping
Aspect of the Hawk
up,
which is a major DPS boost. Beyond that, Taurens still get an additional 5% max health and 1%
hit chance with
Endurance
and an on-use AoE stun with
War Stomp
.
Alliance
: Human –
for the Alliance,
the choice of racials is far closer so you should feel free to pick whichever one fits your personal
preference. However, Humans will offer a slight edge in both PvP and PvE.
Will to Survive
is an invaluable panic button to break stuns, which in PvP is when you are in the most danger against
melee that connect with you.
Perception
also provides another tool to look
for stealthed targets. Finally, the major DPS increase comes from
Sword Specialization
,
which causes you to gain 2% crit chance as long as your melee weapons include at least 1 sword. It is
important to note that this generally increases your crit chance, so it will also apply the bonus to your
ranged attacks.
3.
Marksmanship Hunter Spells and Rotation
The Hunter rotation is incredibly simple early on, almost entirely relying on the strength of
Auto Shot
to kill enemies. First and foremost, always have
Aspect of the Hawk
active before engaging with something unless you are actively kiting it away and need the speed bonus
of
Aspect of the Cheetah
. Before Level 10, you should also focus on moving backwards
between Auto Shots since you want to maximize the number of times you attack a target from range
before it reaches your dead-zone and gets into melee.
Put
Hunter's Mark
up on your target before combat.
Command your pet to attack your target first, with its abilities on auto-cast.
Once your pet damages and attacks your target, start with
Serpent Sting
.
Aimed Shot
on cooldown.
Continue to
Auto Shot
your target.
If you ever pull aggro away from your pet, use
Disengage
.
If you find yourself capped on mana, use
Arcane Shot
.
Auto Shot
the enemy until it dies.
As a final reminder, the majority of a Hunter's power comes from both you and your pet's basic attacks.
Even if you are out of mana, it will always be more efficient to just attack the next target and
regenerate your mana slowly while using basic attacks. Prioritize using
Mend Pet
to heal your pet along with
Serpent Sting
to efficiently utilize your mana.
3.1.
Pets
At Level 10, you will have the ability to tame a pet. This is the single greatest leveling tool
that any class gets without exception. Hunters have always had the ability to tame a pet, but there
are a couple of important distinctions from Classic that are worth noting.
Pets have one of three classifications: Ferocity, Cunning, or Tenacity.
Pets do not have an inherent damage buff or reduction based on type.
Pet happiness and loyalty still exists; remember to feed your pet!
Pets inherit some of your stats, which means they gain power along with you.
Every pet family such as cats or turtles has its own unique ability.
To level up pet abilities, you still need to go out and tame a higher level pet that already
    knows the skill you are looking for. Your pet will not naturally learn higher level abilities on
    its own.
Once you do train higher level pet abilities, you can then teach it to any other pet in the future
	that is capable of learning that ability.
For leveling, Bears are a generally strong choice. They are a defensive pet capable of tanking
well, but most importantly have access to a unique Swipe ability. A Bear's Swipe has a 5-second
cooldown and deals cleave damage in front of them, which makes it one of the rare pet abilities
capable of dealing consistent AoE damage to hold aggro on multiple targets.
3.2.
Utility and Unique Tools
Hunters are known for a variety of unique utility tools that are both incredibly useful
and flavorful for the class.
Hunters can track different types of enemies on the mini-map through various tracking skills.
Hunters can always keep an aspect buff up, which notably includes
Aspect of the Cheetah
.
  This is one of the rare movement speed buffs available before you get a mount.
Feign Death
will cause you to play dead, causing any nearby enemies
  to drop threat on you and reset. However, they will still attack your pet if it is alive and nearby.
  This is one of the most valuable leveling spells for resetting and leaving combat if things get too dangerous.
Freezing Trap
will freeze an enemy in a block of ice when triggered, providing
  a reliable way to keep one target locked down.
Frost Trap
leaves a patch of frost on an area, massively slowing down
  targets inside.
Concussive Shot
is an instant-cast, single-target slow. This is one of the
  strongest tools a Hunter has in PvP, especially against melee.
Disengage
can be used to lower your threat on a target.
4.
Level 30 Gear, Stat Priority, and Consumables
While leveling up to 30, generally you should go for the highest level items that follow the stat
priority listed below. Look out for pieces with high amounts of Agility specifically, high level weapons,
and rare quality gear wherever you can. The best items available will come from a combination
of dungeon quests, dungeon boss drops, crafted pieces, and other quest chain rewards.
At Level 20, some of the best gear comes from the Wailing Caverns dungeon. This includes
the
Venomstrike
bow along with the full Fang set, with pieces such as
Leggings of the Fang
.
At level 30, the difference in most slots is relatively minor as well.  However, there are a few
notable outliers for what is available.
Truthseeker's Bow
is an incredible
low level bow that you can pick up as a quest reward.
Leatherworking
has some strong pieces available from crafting, including the chest
Dusky Leather Armor
.
Triprunner Dungarees
are a quest reward from one of the Gnomeregan
dungeon quests. Finally,
Armor Piercer
gives more Agility than any other weapon
combination and is a common boss drop from Razorfen Kraul.
4.1.
Stat Priority
The stat priority boils down to two things: get the highest damage weapons possible and
get as much Agility as possible. Beyond that, you generally will just want the highest level
gear possible while leveling. Below is a more detailed explanation of the various stats
for Marksmanship Hunter and the benefits they provide.
Weapon Damage
Far and away your most important stat. Keep in mind, weapons have both a DPS value
	and a damage value; slower weapons will hit harder, but less often. While you usually will just
	prefer the higher level weapon, slower weapons are better overall since you want a weapon
	that deals more damage per individual hit. This is because your abilities such as
Aimed Shot
calculate their base damage from your weapon's damage, meaning your abilities do more
	damage with a higher damage weapon.
Hit
You have a baseline chance to miss attacks, which increases as you face higher level enemies.
	Getting hit chance makes you less likely to miss. This stat is strong, but is also generally not
	ever found on low level gear.
Agility
Increases both your attack power and crit chance per point. In general, Hunters gain the
	majority of their scaling from Agility, which makes this your most important primary stat. You
	should be looking to have this on every piece of gear.
Critical Strike
Critical strikes deal bonus damage and provide bonus effects through certain talents, such
	as your
Mortal Shots
talent, which further increases the bonus damage your crits deal.
	Marksmanship relies on critically striking frequently, which makes this highly valuable
	as a stat. However, similar to hit chance, this is not found on lower level gear.
Intellect
Each point provides one Attack Power through
Careful Aim
, while
	also increasing your maximum mana. With Careful Aim talented this is your next most important
	stat after Agility. Having a higher mana pool is also incredibly important generally just
	to ensure you can cast more spells without stopping in a single fight.
Spirit
Increases your base mana regeneration and your out of combat health regeneration rates.
	This is a valuable leveling stat since it will cause you to recover more
	mana faster. However, this is only for leveling; Stamina and Intellect are far more valuable
	for both survivability and actual combat capacity.
Stamina
Each point increases your maximum health. Having a large health pool is important
	for just being more durable, but as a Hunter you generally should not be tanking or taking
	damage. This is your least important stat while leveling.
4.2.
Consumables
While leveling, the most important consumables are going to be the highest level food you
can eat for health regeneration, water for mana regeneration, and health potions as an emergency
defensive button. While you can look into elixirs and other buff foods, you do not need to focus
on them too much while leveling unless you are trying to optimize significantly.
That being said, there are some easy elixirs you can get to help with your base power while
leveling.
Elixir of Agility
along with other variations of the straight Agility
elixirs are going to be the most noticeable damage increase, and quite cost efficient while leveling
once you have some gold to spare. Since you are leveling with a pet, you do not need to worry
too much about survivability; any buffs should primarily focus on damage.
Another important consumable will be bandages from
First Aid
. First
Aid gives you something to use your cloth on while leveling, and provides an incredibly strong
way of healing yourself both in and out of combat. It is highly recommended to keep your First
Aid skill current while leveling.
4.3.
Campfire Buffs
One of the incredible new additions in World of Wacraft Forever is campsites. You can
set up Campsites yourself, or look for them out in the world to sit by a campfire for the campfire
buffs. Different professions can offer buffs, all of which generally correspond to the possible
class buffs. These are incredibly strong while leveling, so if you ever seen players sitting around
a campfire out in the world, make sure to stop by to sit and get some buffs.

Requires pet management, especially in dungeons/raids, to avoid pulling additional enemies
Best Specialization For Leveling A Hunter
Hunters are one of the easiest and most efficient classes to level in WoW Forever. We have great damage both in ST and AoE, and good utility with our traps. Overall,
Beast Mastery is our preferred option for leveling
.
Beast Mastery is an amazing choice for any player, but especially solo levelers. The spec revolves around keeping your pet alive as it does incredible damage and tanks enemies, all while you fire off abilities from afar without ever taking damage - this reduces the risk of death significantly compared to other DPS specs, especially when talented into survivability.
Recommended Leveling Talents for Hunter
The following is my recommended Talent Build for leveling in WoW Forever:
If you prefer slightly more DPS in exchange for survivability, you can put your 2nd point of
Improved Revive Pet
into
Ferocity
instead, along with your
Intimidation
and
Bestial Swiftness
for a total of 5/5
Ferocity
. However, we recommend taking these talents for the additional survivability and utility, as
Ferocity
is a relatively small DPS buff.
Legacy Talents:
In the beta, we can get up to 5 extra talent points using the "Talented" Legacy Talent. The below talents include these additional 5 points. Check out our
Legacy Talents
guide to learn more!
Level 60:
This section will be updated to show the suggested Talents to level 60 in due course!
Best Races for Hunter in WoW Forever
Alliance: Human or Night Elf
For Alliance, we recommend playing a Human or Night Elf Hunter. The new
Human Hunter
is a great choice, as
Ruthless
provides a flat 2% crit chance, which is a great passive DPS increase. Additionally,
The Human Spirit
provides a helpful 5% Spirit (albeit not incredibly important for Hunters), and
Will To Survive
immediately removes all stuns, acting as a very useful defensive.
Perception
can also be helpful against some enemies, or for PvP against classes with stealth i.e. Rogues.
Night Elves
are also a very powerful race for Hunters. The new racial
Elune's Light
gives 10% crit chance for 15 seconds, which is a significant damage increase on use and
Quickness
provides some extra survivability and movement speed passively, which is always helpful.
Shadowmeld
is incredibly useful when questing. When used out of combat it allows you to remain stealthed as long as you are stationary so you can use this stealth to eat/drink without risk. When used outside of combat it has a 10 second cooldown. Inside combat, it drops you to the bottom of the threat table against anything you're fighting, meaning your party members or pet are guaranteed to take aggro over you on use. When used during combat it has a 2 minute cooldown. If things go wrong,
Wisp Spirit
will help you return to your body fast!
Horde: Orc
For Horde, we recommend playing an Orc Hunter.
Orc Hunters
provide a very strong on-use button with
Blood Fury
, giving 10% Attack Power for 15 seconds, which greatly scales damage both for you and your pet(s). On top of this they feature
Savage
which provides a passive 1% crit chance.
Their remaining two racials are strong defensives in
Hardiness
, reducing the duration of all stuns by 20%, and
Shatter Curse
, which immediately removes all Curses and Banes, and reduces incoming magic damage by 5% for 8 seconds.
Hunter Playstyle and Core Abilities for Leveling
Your goal as a Beast Mastery Hunter while leveling is to keep your distance and burn enemies down before they can hit you. Prior to level 10, you achieve this via kiting, and using
Concussive Shot
from level 8 onwards to slow enemies, all while getting as many
Auto Shots
off as possible and the occasional
Arcane Shot
.
After level 10, our pet begins to tank for us, and we can simply keep our distance and burn enemies down, eventually using
Aimed Shot
/
Multi-Shot
for optimal DPS, all while our pet hits them in melee.
Once we reach level 25, we have to juggle our
Summon Hawk
casts along with our normal pet management, ideally keeping 2 hawks and our normal pet out at all times for optimal DPS. This is very important, and we should try not to recast
Summon Hawk
before the last second the hawk is active so as to conserve mana and spend our GCDs on useful abilities.
We can also use our traps to help us keep our distance in sticky situations, and
Feign Death
to escape bad situations where we're in combat.
Key Spells & Leveling Milestones for Hunter
Our most important Level during leveling is easily 10, unlocking our pet, along with
Aspect Of The Hawk
. Aside from this we have a good spread of important spells across the leveling process, with solid spikes at levels 18, 20, and 25 via
Multi-Shot
,
Aimed Shot
, and
Summon Hawk
respectively.
You should upgrade spells mentioned below whenever you get the opportunity to as higher ranks are almost always a better choice - the levels listed are for the first rank. The exceptions to this are
Raptor Strike
, which loses almost all value after level 10, and
Arcane Shot
, which becomes near redundant after level 25 unless fighting an enemy in ST for 12 seconds or more.
Spell
Level
Impact
Raptor Strike

A buffed melee. This is still worth less than an
Auto Shot
, but before level 10 is useful when in unavoidable melee encounters. Kiting is always better.
Serpent Sting
4
Our first ranged spell is a DoT we use all the way to max level. Not worth using if the target will die fast as it has no upfront damage.
Arcane Shot

Summon Hawk

Summon Hawk

Pet Abilities -
Growl
,
Great Stamina
,
Natural Armor
10
Our first pet abilities are available immediately upon taming our first pet. Make sure these are learned + trained, and that your pet is using
Growl

and
Natural Armor
are passive survivability increases for our pet.

Aimed Shot

Multi-Shot
. Does incredible ST damage in exchange for a long 2 second cast.
Aspect Of The Cheetah
20
30% movement speed. This should be used at all times when traversing without a mount and not fighting enemies.
Freezing Trap
20
A 10 second hard CC which is broken by damage. Great for creating distance from enemies or escaping bad situations. Shares a cooldown with
Frost Trap
.
Track Hidden
24
While all of our tracking spells are decent, this one is incredible. Bonus stealth detection is great generally, and being able to track stealthed enemies is very useful for some quests.
Summon Hawk
25
A new ability in Forever,
Summon Hawk
effectively gives us 2 more pets to manage. Having both of these hawks out as much as possible without refreshing too early is core for our DPS, and as they last 18 seconds, this should often be easy to manage. This ability is learned as a talent. Shares a 6 second cooldown with
Arcane Shot
.
Rapid Fire
26
Our first "real" cooldown ability. Great burst damage on a 5 minute cooldown.
Frost Trap
28
Slows all enemies in its area of effect by a whopping 60%. Incredibly useful, especially for AoE pulls where our pet may not be able to maintain aggro on all targets. Shares a cooldown with
Freezing Trap
.
Intimidation
30
A 3 second stun with some bonus damage from our pet as a cherry on top. Also useful as an alternative taunt from our pet to pull enemies off of us due to the high threat generation. This ability is learned as a talent.
Feign Death
30
Removes us from combat with anything currently attacking us. One of the most useful abilities in the game, but bear in mind this can miss/be dodged like any other attack, so be careful!
Pet Ability -
Dash
30
Grants our pet 40% movement speed for 15 seconds. A solid DPS increase by letting our pet move to targets significantly faster.
This ability is learned via Wild Taming.
Tame a pet that knows
Dash
and use it in combat until you see the "You have learned a new spell" system message in chat. At this point, you can now teach it to any pet you'd like!
Best / Suggested Professions for Hunter
Profession 1: Leatherworking
We recommend Leatherworking as your first profession. With the new BoP profession items in Forever, the ability to make your own leather gear is even more valuable than ever. Starting from level 10 you can make your own blue leveling gear with large amounts of Agility that directly buffs our DPS greatly.
For example,
Brawler's Leather Helm
is an incredibly strong piece with a huge amount of Agility on it, and is BiS for us during the beta. Also, Leatherworking is fully mobile unlike other crafting professions that need anvils or similar, meaning you can make your own gear on the go without having to return to town provided you have the materials.
Profession 2: Skinning
For a second profession, we suggest Skinning. Skinning feeds directly into our Leatherworking profession, and saves us from having to spend large amounts repetitively on the Auction House to train Leatherworking and eventually craft our BoP items. Additionally, any spare hides can be sold for a tidy profit, whether to vendors or other players.
Because the majority of our damage also comes from our pet, Skinning synergises well with Hunter DPS, as we can send our pet to begin attacking our next target while we skin, minimizing downtime that other classes often would see as a downside from Skinning.
Secondary Professions
Don't neglect your secondary professions either! With the profession changes in Forever, Cooking is providing some of the best food in the game, even giving XP buffs!
First Aid is great to get you out of a pinch, especially as a class with
Freezing Trap
giving you a chance to get a full-length bandage off if needed.
Fishing can make decent money selling what you catch, or can be used to train your Cooking up even further.
Hunter Leveling Tips & Tricks
Maximising Auto Shots
Auto Shot
is a significant portion of our damage across all levels, but especially early. Maximising the amount of
Auto Shots
you can get on an enemy is one of the easiest and most impactful ways to improve your DPS while leveling as a Hunter, and utilising kiting, slows, and pet taunts cannot be overstated as an incredibly important thing to focus on while playing your Hunter.
Managins Pet Threat
At certain points during the leveling process, you might find yourself pulling aggro from your pet if you begin attacking enemies immediately. To solve this, it's better to let your pet get a few attacks in before you begin your ranged DPS. This feels like an error, but you'll do more damage staying in ranged, even while missing a few attacks, compared to if enemies are allowed to enter melee range of you.
Train as often as possible, and good luck!
We hope our Hunter Leveling guide for WoW Forever was useful to help you know where to spend your talent points and how to get the most out of the class whilst leveling. This guide will be updated to cover 1-60 when the full game releases and as more information becomes available, so keep checking back in!

Introduction
Welcome to our Shaman Leveling Guide for World of Warcraft Forever. This guide will cover everything you need to know to level a Shaman in WoW Forever, including an overview of Shaman Strengths and Weaknesses, a Leveling Talents Build for Shaman, and the best Professions for a Shaman.

Other Shaman Leveling Info
Strengths & Weaknesses of Shaman in WoW Forever
Strengths
Solid damage and self-sustain.
Can DPS, tank, and heal dungeons.
Ghost Wolf
makes you very quick and mobile.
Totems give you a lot of utility, such as slows, AOE, healing, mana regen, and more.
Weaknesses
No crowd control.
Unpredictable damage, as your damage is tied to Windfury procs.
Recommended Leveling Talents for Shaman in WoW Forever
There are a few key talents you can look forward to in the early stages of your leveling journey.
Improved Ghost Wolf
reduces the cast time of
Ghost Wolf
, making it an instant cast when you have 2/2 points in the talent. You want to make sure you have 2/2 points in this Talent before reaching level 20, as that's when you learn
Ghost Wolf
.
At level 25, you can get
Stormstrike
, which makes your damage rotation much more engaging.
Shaman Playstyle and Core Abilities
Enhancement is the strongest leveling specialization for Shamans in WoW: Forever. You’re a melee spec with a ton of utility from your totems, off-heals, and
Earth Shock
, which has a triple function as damage spell, taunt and interrupt.
Basic Rotation
For the most part, you’ll be pulling one mob at a time. Your basic rotation is pretty simple: apply
Flame Shock
, drop
Searing Totem
, and start meleeing while using
Frost Shock
or
Earth Shock
when they’re available. Re-apply
Flame Shock
once the DoT runs out.
Levels 1-30
You’ll generally want to use either a 2H or a 1H + shield with
Rockbiter Weapon
on your weapon.
Rockbiter Weapon
gives you a huge amount of Attack Power at these levels and is much better than
Flametongue Weapon
or
Frostbrand Weapon
.
Levels 30+
Once you hit 30, you’ll want to switch to a 2H with
Windfury Weapon
. When
Windfury Weapon
procs, it can hit extremely hard, and honestly, there’s not much more satisfying than watching those big numbers pop up.
Key Abilities
Flame Shock
,
Frost Shock
, and
Earth Shock
all have their own uses. For pure damage, you can switch between them depending on which ranks you have available at your current level.
Earth Shock
is especially useful as your interrupt, while
Frost Shock
gives you a slow when you need it.
Earthbind Totem
is also incredibly useful. You can drop it to kite mobs, or use it to stop mobs from running away when they’re low on health. It’s especially useful in dungeons, for mob control.
Fire Nova
is your main burst AoE ability. It deals a large amount of Fire damage around the Fire Totem you have placed, making it great when you have multiple mobs stacked together, but also deals solid single target damage.
Ghost Wolf
is fantastic from levels 20-39. With
Improved Ghost Wolf
, it becomes an instant cast and gives you 40% movement speed, making you one of the fastest classes in Azeroth between those levels.
Rage Of The Farseer
is a personal Bloodlust. It gives you both attack speed and cast speed, making it incredibly powerful. You can use it to burst down mobs, get some extra healing out when you’re in trouble, or simply take on slightly larger pulls than you normally would.

Best / Suggested Professions for Shaman
Profession 1: Leatherworking
Lets you craft very powerful gear while leveling, such as
Dark Leather Boots
around level 10,
Brawler's Leather Hood
around level 20.
Profession 2: Skinning
Allows you to collect the required materials to craft your leatherworking gear.
Secondary Professions
Cooking allows you to make food which gives you a 15-minute buff that increases experience gained from killing mobs by 5%.
First aid lets you make bandages which are a great way to heal yourself when you’re low on mana and don’t want to sit around waiting for it to regenerate.
Other Shaman Specific Leveling Info
Stat Prio:
Agility > Strength > Stamina > Intellect
If you're on the PvP server and experiencing World PvP, I suggest aiming for gear with Stamina combined with Agility, Strength, or Intellect.
Don't be afraid to tank dungeons as a Shaman while leveling, so long as you have access to a 1-hander and shield. You generate solid threat with
Rockbiter Weapon
and
Earth Shock.
Fire Nova
now generates threat to you instead of your
Searing Totem
and
Magma Totem
compared to original Classic, which enables you to generate decent AOE threat.
We hope our Shaman Leveling guide for WoW Forever was useful to help you know where to spend your talent points and how to get the most out of the class whilst leveling.
